key_insight: Acoustic forcing can drive very different mesoscale flame regimes into a shared oscillatory ignition-extinction state (O-FREI), with stronger forcing reducing mean heat release while amplifying forcing-frequency oscillations.
engineering_relevance: Understanding how confinement and acoustic forcing destabilize mesoscale flames helps design more robust micro-combustors and portable power systems that must operate under unsteady flow conditions.
method: Applied upstream acoustic forcing at the combustor’s first harmonic across a wide range of pressure intensities.
Compared three flame regimes: FREI, stable flames, and propagating flames.
Used reduced-order mathematical models to interpret the observed transitions and oscillation dynamics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports regime-dependent responses that converge to O-FREI at higher forcing, including lower mean heat release, stronger forcing-frequency oscillations, and reduced Strouhal number for ignition-extinction cycles.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on a confined mesoscale combustor and first-harmonic forcing, so the observed transition may not generalize directly to other geometries, fuels, or forcing spectra.
paper_title: Response of Confined Mesoscale Flames to Acoustic Forcing
